Commentary.Commentary: OKAY. Finally we get to know. BANGLADESH ARE BATTING AGAIN. Imrul Kayes and Liton Das are the openers. Kyle Jarvis will start off proceedings. Liton to face. Here we go!

Time now for a chat with Bangladesh's coach Sunil Joshi. Feels that coaching Bangladesh is not about what the coaching manual says but what Bangladesh need. Adds that Test cricket is a matter of patience and the hosts will have to be patient to win the game. On Taijul Islam, Joshi is proud of the way he has been working 18 months on bowling in consistent areas and admires his mindset. On warming up for the game, Sunil says that there are a different set of routines to do those, as opposed to a limited overs game and reckons that Taijul has been doing that well.

Brendan Taylor is having a chat with Tino Mawoyo. Says that he enjoyed the challenge and feels it is a nice feeling to have got the century but admits that there is a log of work to do. Does not want to compare himself with Andy Flower, adding that he has a lot of cricket to play to even think of reaching that level. Just wants to take it game by game for now. On the conditions, Brendan feels that for the first half of yesterday, they were pretty fine and it was more of Bangladesh's incisive bowling which made run-scoring difficult. Admits that Sikandar Raza missed out on the first innings but is pretty sure that he will bounce back. Agrees that he is disappointed with the shot he played to get out (himself).

PITCH REPORT - Tino Mawoyo doing the pitch report observes that there is some degradation on the surface, though there is some covering of grass. But it will be just a matter of time before they open up. Batting will only get difficult.

Looking forward to the day, this is Day 4 and the day where pitches in the subcontinent really open up and help spinners wreck havoc. Batting won't be easy and don't think we will see pace bowlers bowling a lot of overs today. Taijul, Mehidy or Mavuta, Williams and Raza might be seen doing the bulk of the bowling depending on Bangladesh's decision.

But just when it looked like Zimbabwe would manage to remove the option for the hosts to enforce the follow-on, they lost wickets in a flurry towards the end of the day. Considering Bangladesh are trailing in the series and have to win to ensure parity, they might just be looking at asking Zimbabwe to bat again. But on the other hand, their bowlers have been on the field for the entirety of a day and might be a bit jaded. Also, they have the Windies series coming up in a week. So all these thoughts must have kept Mahmudullah and Co. pondering over what to do.

Hello and Welcome to Day 4 of the second Test between Bangladesh and Zimbabwe in Mirpur. The past 3 days have seen the conclusion of the first innings of both teams. Bangladesh batted deep into Day 2 and hoped they would have to bat only once in this match. They still might do it but the chances of that look slimmer than they did post their first innings. Zimbabwe started Day 3 at 25/1 after managing to escape the 18 overs on the Day 2 evening without much damage. They lost early wickets in the first session and the first half of the second session but then had a big partnership that rescued them.
... Day 4, Session 1 ...

Now we head into Day 4 with the biggest question in mind - Will Bangladesh enforce the follow-on? We will find out the answer on Wednesday at 0930 local (0330 GMT). Do join us for all the updates. Till then, goodbye and take care.

Earlier, the tourists entered Day 3 on the back foot and were further pegged back as their top and middle order failed to contribute. They were reeling at 131-5 at one stage but a century stand between Taylor and Moor revived hopes of a comeback and avoiding the follow-on. But a flurry of wickets towards the end saw Bangladesh finishing Day 3 in firm control of this Test match.

Zimbabwe continued their fightback in the last session with Moor and Taylor adding a brilliant 139-run stand. Both looked set to score big but Bangladesh struck through Ariful Haque, a part-timer. He got rid of Moor and then the wickets just kept falling. Mehidy got two in one over, which included the prized wicket of Brendan Taylor. Taijul Islam finished things off in the end and bagged a fifer.

Right then, after all the hard work, Bangladesh have managed to shot out Zimbabwe's first innings. Now, it will be interesting to see if they enforce the follow-on. They have never done so in the past but they might just do it here. The hosts have a lead of 218 runs and batting again will take more time out of the game. Keeping in mind that they are trailing in the series, this is surely going to be a tough decision as they bowled 105.3 overs and their bowlers will be tired. Mahmudullah has a full night to think about it.

OUT! It is a clean catch and that is the end of Zimbabwe's innings as Chatara won't be able to bat. Islam gets his sixth fifer in Tests, third in a row. Simply amazing. He tosses it up around middle and it comes in with the angle. Chakabva tries to defend with his bat way ahead of his front pad. The ball goes off the inner half towards Mominul at short leg. He is standing nice and low and he seems to have taken it. The players start celebrating but the umpire wants it to be checked. He takes it upstairs and replays show that the catch is clean as a whistle. Zimbabwe's first innings is over and that also will be STUMPS ON DAY 3!
Appeal for a bat-pad! Bangladesh are celebrating, it's a fifer for Taijul. Umpire Dharmasena though wants it to be checked. Soft signal is out. Let's see...
Loopy ball outside off, Chakabva strokes it to covers.

NOT OUT! Umpire's call as it is clipping the top of the stumps. It is pitched around middle and then skids through. Chakabva tries to work it on the leg side but misses to get hit high on the pads. An appeal follows and the umpire shakes his head. Bangladesh take the review and the replays show that the on-field call will stay.
Another review from Bangladesh! Chakabva is the man in question. Looks a touch high.

DROPPED AGAIN! This time by Liton Das at short leg. Full and flighted on the middle stump, Jarvis plays the flick shot but it goes in and out of the short leg fielder's hands. So two drops in the same over and Jarvis the survivor on both occasions!
Flatter ball outside off and turning in towards the batsman. Chakabva makes room and pushes it to deep extra cover for a run.
Fuller ball outside off, Jarvis drives to cover and picks up another single.
DROPPED! Very tough chance. Full ball on the pads, Jarvis wants to play it on the leg side toward the mid-wicket region but hits it straight at forward short leg, who can't latch onto it.
Loopy ball outside off, Jarvis attempts the drive but gets a thick edge towards third man. The batsmen manage to run two.
Flatter ball on a good length and on middle, Chakabva plays it to square leg for a single.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
This is flatter and on off, Jarvis goes back and defends it.
Loopy ball on the stumps, the batsman pushes it back to the bowler.
Flighted on the stumps, it is blocked out solidly.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On the stumps, kept out.
Slightly faster on a length, Chakabva wants to open the face of the bat and guide it towards third man, but gets an edge that drops just short of slip. Risky attempt.
Flatter ball on the stumps, jabbed away by Chakabva to short mid-wicket. No run taken though.
Flatter and on the stumps. Chakabva defends off his back foot.

Dropped? No. Flatter and outside off, Jarvis wanted to hit to mid-wicket but gets the inside half of the bat and hits it in the air. Mehidy dives across to his right but it falls wide. The ball runs down to long on after that and the batsmen get a single.
Loopy ball on a length and on middle stump, Chakabva plays it behind square leg for a run.
Mehidy from around the wicket bowls it flat and on a length outside off, Jarvis punches it to long on for a single.
Flatter on off, kept out safely to end a quick over.
Fires this on the pads, it is worked through square leg for another run.
On the pads, this is worked around the corner for a run.
On the stumps, kept out.
Outside off, left alone.
Full and flighted on off stump, Chakabva defends it with a straight bat.
This is given air outside off, it pitches and turns back in. Jarvis lunges forward to defend but is beaten by the turn. The ball hits his pads. An appeal follows but not given. Impact outside off.
Loopy ball on off, it is blocked solidly.
Down the leg side, it is tucked away through backward square leg for a couple.
On the stumps, Kyle keeps it out.
There is a chat between the two batsmen, not sure about what.
Flatter and on off, the batsman goes back and defends it out.
Tosses it up on off, the batsman works it towards mid-wicket.

Bangladesh have six balls at Jarvis next over as the batsmen run through for a single. The ball was full, fast and on the leg stump, Jarvis plays it all along the ground to deep mid-wicket for a single.
Slightly fuller than a good length, Chakabva just plays it fine on the leg side and runs for one.
Flatter and quicker this time, Chakabva goes onto his back foot and defends it back to the bowler.
Full and flighted again, Chakabva defends it back to the bowler off the back foot.
Overpitched and almost yorker length. Chakabva plays it to short mid-wicket. No run.
Flighted and on the stumps, Chakabva defends it with a straight bat.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat. A double-wicket maiden for Mehidy!
Gives it air on off, Jarvis blocks it.
Floats it up on off, it is kept out.
Kyle Jarvis is the number 10 batsman and should be the last one also with Tendai Chatara not expected to bat.

OUT! One brings two! Now they have only 2 wickets in hand (count it one with Chatara not expected to bat) and need another 33 to avoid the follow-on. The straighter one does the trick. It is tossed up around off, Mavuta plays inside the line, thinking it would turn into him. It does not and takes the outside edge. Ariful Haque makes no mistake at first slip and Mavuta goes for a duck.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Brandon Mavuta is the new man in.

OUT! What a catch that is! Something special was needed to get rid of Taylor and Taijul has provided it. He has pulled off an absolute screamer. Taylor has nailed the sweep shot. It is right off the middle, he must have thought there are runs on offer as soon as he hit it but it was not to be. Islam in the deep square leg region is standing a bit ahead of the rope and dives to his right to grab a two-handed stunner. Outstanding. End of a magnificent knock but Zimbabwe needed him to stay out there. 33 more runs needed to avoid the follow-on.
Another ball which pitches and comes back in. It is worked to mid-wicket.
Good length again on off, the batter works it with the angle to mid-wicket.
On a length around off, it is blocked.
An outswinger but it is outside off, left alone.
Good length again around off, kept out.
Good length on the middle pole, the batsman gets behind the line and keeps it out.
Full and on the pads, Chakabva tucks it away behind square leg for a single and keeps the strike.
Comes around the wicket for this ball, Chakabva lets the ball go through outside off stump with the angle.
Full and flighted on the stumps, kept out easily by Chakabva.
Slower ball outside off, no turn at all. Chakabva defends with soft hands. No run.
Flighted delivery on the off stump, Chakabva keeps it out.
Length ball outside off, no turn on it. Taylor mistimes the drive but it goes in the gap and they pick up a single.
Mehidy Hasan is back on.
The batsman has driven it to mid on.
Back of a length on off, kept out.

FOUR! A valiant effort in the deep by Rahman but it goes in vain. Full and on the pads, Chakabva flicks it through square leg. Mustafizur from fine leg runs to his left, dives and tries to pull it back in. The umpire goes upstairs to check but replays show that the ball was in contact with Rahman's body as he touched the ropes.
Good length ball on off stump, Chakabva defends that straight.

NOT OUT! Yes, it is going down leg! Good length ball starting on middle and moving down the leg. Chakabva tries to flick but misses and gets hit on the pads. The players appeal but the umpire shakes his head. Bangladesh take the review. Hawk Eye shows the ball to be missing the stumps and Bangladesh lose a review. Pretty poor review, to be honest!
Howzzat? The answer to that question is not out. An appeal for an LBW has been turned down. Chakabva is the man in question. Looks like it will be missing leg.
Good length ball on the stumps, Chakabva tries to play it to the leg side to get off the mark but finds the fielder.

FOUR! Consecutive boundaries! And the runs needed to avoid the follow-on is below 40. This is fired outside off, Taylor gets into position early and reverse sweeps it through short third man. A boundary results.
FOUR! Conventional sweep and he gets the desired result. Goes down on one knee and sweeps it over the mid-wicket region for a boundary.
Goes for the reverse sweep but misses. Easy Taylor, you can't just throw your wicket away.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Flatter around off, it is kept out.

100 for Taylor. What a knock it has been! His first away from home and his 5th overall in Tests. A very important knock. He came out when Zimbabwe were in big trouble and has held the fort at one end. Islam tosses this up around middle, Taylor goes for the hoick but gets it off the inner half through mid-wicket. The batsmen run two. Taylor takes his helmet off and acknowledges the applause from his teammates. He though would know he can't just relax. Still a long way to go. For the record, it's a century from his bat after a gap of five years.
BEATEN! Good length around off, it straightens a touch. Haque plays inside the line and gets beaten.
Back of a length on off, the batsman defends it off the front foot.
Way outside off again, looking to get it back in. No swing though and it has been left alone.
Length and outside off, it is left alone.
Good length again on off, the batsman gets behind the line of the delivery and keeps it out.
Shortish and around off, Chakabva works it towards square leg.
Similar ball and kept out by Taylor by showing the full face of the bat. The hundred will have to wait for another over.
Fuller and quicker through the air, defended off the front foot by Taylor.
Full ball on the stumps and Taylor defends it straight back to the bowler.
FOUR! Taylor lifts it beautifully over extra cover and in the gap for a boundary. He moves to 99 now. Just a single away from a superb century.
Fuller and on off stump, Taylor plays it toward short mid-wicket again. No run.
Good length ball on the stumps. Defended towards mid-wicket by Taylor.
Drinks break. Meanwhile, Regis Chakabva has joined Brendan Taylor in the middle.

OUT! Three reds and Bangladesh have finally broken the 139-run stand. Much-needed wicket for the hosts and a timely one. Zimbabwe are still 53 runs away from avoiding the follow-on and they have 4 more wickets in hand. Haque bowls it on the fuller side and it jags back in late. Moor fails to adjust to the swing as he tries to work it on the leg side. Misses completely and it hits his front pad. It goes to the keeper who takes it and appeals. The Bangladesh players are appealing for both, an LBW and a caught behind. The umpire though raises his finger, which we think is for Leg Before Wicket. Moor though reviews it. Replays detect no inside edge but Hawk Eye shows three reds. Peter walks back after an excellent knock although he will be disappointed to miss out on a ton. Zimbabwe lose their review as well. Bangladesh are ecstatic. Credit to Mahmudullah to bring Ariful into the attack, he ain't a regular bowler but has done the job.
Big moment in the game! Moor has been given out LBW. He though has reviewed.
Short and wide outside off, Taylor cuts it to sweeper cover for another single.
Length ball outside off, Moor pushes it to the cover region for a run.
Good length ball on off stump. It keeps low but Moor defends it well.
Short and outside off, Moor guides it square on the off side for another couple.
Gentle medium pace sliding down the leg side, Moor plays it fine on the leg side for a couple.
Interesting. Ariful Haque has been given a fairly new nut by Mahmudullah.
Tossed up ball on middle, played off the pads to mid-wicket.

Dropped! Yet another chance goes down abegging! This time Mushfiqur Rahim is the culprit. Quicker delivery again, around off and spinning away just a bit. Taylor is forward to defend but it takes a faint outside edge and goes quickly behind to the keeper. Rahim fails to hold on to the catch. Now, both batsmen have got a reprieve each. Sloppy from the hosts.
Fires one in the blockhole, Taylor does well to dig it out back to the bowler.
Straighter in line, calmly nudged in the gap on the leg side for a single.
Gets forward to a full ball and eases it past the bowler and through mid off again for one.
Knocks a full ball down to long off for a run.
Bouncer again. The best of the lot. Taylor in two minds and decides to leave it alone very late. It was very close to the glove. Rahim goes up in an appeal. But the umpire isn't interested.
Slower delivery just outside off, Taylor defends it straight back to the mid off region.

Short ball again aimed at the batsman's body, cramping him for room. Taylor adjusts well and defends it onto the leg side. No run though. Taylor wanted a run but sent back by the non striker. The fielder has a shy at striker's end but to no avail.
Good length this time. It was a slower ball but read by Taylor and defended with the full face of the bat.
Short of a good length again, Moor rocks back and plays it square on the off side for a run.
Short ball on the leg side, Taylor fends it off awkwardly behind square on the leg side and picks up a run.
Flatter and on middle, Moor goes back and punches it towards the fielder on the leg side.
Moor has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Too full and on off, Moor strokes it hard but straight to the cover fielder.
Slower through the air and it lands full around off, Taylor gets forward and drives it down the ground to long off for one.
Flighted again, it's outside off and Brendan leaves it alone.
Flighted and full outside off, driven off the front foot to the cover fielder.

DROPPED! This ball holds up in the pitch again, and Moor goes through with the cover drive and is early into it. It goes up in the air. Very difficult chance to hold on for Nazmul Islam, the substitute fielder. He leaps and gets his left hand to it but can't hold on. The ball was always going away from him but he should have done better, especially after getting his hands to it.
Short ball again but Moor ducks out of the way of the ball this time.
Good length ball outside off, Moor just drops the ball onto the ground.

FOUR! Much finer this time. Was a short ball from Mustafizur, didn't bounce as much as expected but Moor stays on the back foot and just lifts the ball over the first slip fielder for a boundary. Brilliant innovation.
Good length ball on the leg stump, Moor defends it watchfully.

FOUR! Not entirely in control but well played in the end. The ball was short and aimed at the body, Moor is on his back foot and just opens the face of his bat. The ball goes between the slips for four runs.
On the middle pole, it is kept out.
BEATEN! Well bowled! This is tossed up around off, it drifts back in due to which the batsman has to play at it. Pitches and then turns away. Beats the outside edge of the batsman.
Fires it on the pads, Moor tries to flick but gets an inside edge onto his pads. It though goes uppishly past the fielder at short leg for a run.
Driven towards the mid off region. The batsmen have run through for a single.
Loopy ball but in the fuller zone again, it is pushed through mid off for a run.
Misfield! Taijul has been guilty of bowling a little too full here in his new spell. Once again it is right up there. The batsman times it towards covers. The fielder misfields and a run is taken.

Overpitched outside off and Taylor plays a really good cover drive and finds the gap between mid off and cover. The ball doesn't reach the boundary and it's a long chase for Taijul who chased it from mid off. The batsmen pick up the third run on the throw as the fielder was late in releasing the ball.
Yorker length ball outside off, Taylor gets the bottom part of his bat on it and the ball goes in the gap straight down the ground. They manage to come back for the second.
Full and just outside off, Taylor covers the line of the ball and drives it straight. No run available though.
Length ball on the stumps, Taylor gets behind the line of the ball and defends it well.

What happened there? The ball seems to have got stuck in the pitch as it brings a puff of dust on landing. Taylor wants to drive the ball down the ground and is early into his shot. The ball is in the air but away from Mustafizur and lands safely in the end. No run taken.
Good length ball on the off stump, defended solidly back to the bowler by Taylor.
Change of ends for Mustafizur Rahman.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
This is on the stumps, it is kept out.
Flighted ball on off, Taylor times it through mid off and another run results.
Fires it on middle, the batsman blocks it out.
Another full toss, this though is quicker and on off. Eased down to long off for a run.

A full toss to begin with. Taylor tries to whip it but his one hand comes off the handle. It goes off the lower portion of the bat and through mid-wicket. Hasan gives it a chase, he collects the ball and almost collides with the fielder coming in from deep square leg. Three taken by the batsmen.
Taijul Islam is back on.

Khaled comes around the wicket for the last delivery, gets it up in the yorker length. Moor is up to the task and keeps it out pretty comfortably. Actually wanted to drive it but was too full for him to execute the shot.
Good length outside the off stump, Taylor stays back to defend this towards cover. They pick up a quick run.
Slightly full and on the middle stump, Moor plays it with soft hands to the mid-wicket region for a run.

FOUR! Slightly overpitched and Moor immediately takes advantage, he drives it beautifully through extra cover for a well-timed four. This also brings up the 100-run stand between these two. What a vital time to get it too! Just 89 more runs required to avoid the follow-on.
Slightly short of a good length outside off, Taylor defends it into the gap in the cover region and picks a single.
Good length ball on target. Taylor is solid in defense though.

FOUR! Easy-peasy! The two now look in no problem whatsoever! Rahman comes around the wicket and bowls it very full around off, Moor opens the face of the bat and guides it through point. No fielder there so a boundary results.
Shortens his length from the previous ball and lands it on off, it is kept out.

A loose shot that! Taylor tries to play it a little away from his body as he tries to force it through the off side. The ball sticks a touch in the surface and hence, goes off the inner half towards mid-wicket. A run taken.
On the shorter side but does not bounce high enough. Taylor works it comfortably towards square leg.
Lands it on leg and then gets it to slant away. Taylor gets behind the line of the delivery and keeps it out.
Down the leg side, Taylor flicks it but finds the man at leg gully.

On good length and drifting on to the leg stump, Taylor plays it wristily to the leg side. The fielder tries getting across to it but then the square leg umpire shows off his football skills and pushes it out. A run is completed.
Length ball coming in to the body, Moor plays it towards the vacant mid-wicket region and picks up an easy run.
Good length ball on the stumps, defended back to the bowler by Moor on the back foot.
Slightly short of good length drifting onto the pads, Taylor tucks it away behind square on the leg side for a single.
Fuller ball at the stumps, driven down to the left of mid off, slightly in the air but safe. The batsmen run one.
Good length ball outside off stump, swinging away! Loose shot attempted by Moor, just throwing his bat at it and misses.
Khaled Ahmed to bowl from the other end.
A dot to end! A good over though for Zimbabwe. Rahman goes back to bowling length and it is blocked out.

FOUR! Top stuff! Two top class boundaries in this over! This one is through the cover region. Full and outside, in fact a half volley. Taylor is too good a batsman to miss out there. He strokes it through covers and the ball races away.
Good length around off, this one stays a touch low. Taylor lunges and keeps it out.
Back of a length on off, Taylor keeps it out off the back foot.

FOUR! DELIGHTFUL! That is a shot by a man in full control. Full and on middle, it shapes back in a touch. Taylor this time does not plant his front foot too across and hence is in great position to play it with the full face of the bat. It is hit past mid on for a boundary.
HUGE APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! Good length delivery angling towards the stumps, Taylor wants to flick towards the leg side but gets hit on the pads. The umpire shakes his head. It pitched outside leg.
The second new ball has been taken straightaway and Mustafizur Rahman is brought back on.
Flighted ball on middle, it is driven to mid off.
On the stumps, it is kept out.

FOUR! UP AND OVER! Gets to his fifty in style! Got a fifty in the first innings of the first Test and now gets one in the first innings here. His 5th in this format. His eyes lit up as he sees the flight on the ball. Lofts it over the mid off fielder and a boundary results. No real celebration as he knows his team is still way behind in the game. However, his partnership with Taylor is reviving some hope for the tourists.
Gives it a nice loop but it lands in the fuller length area, stroked down to long on for a run.
Slows it up this time but no real turn for Hasan. It goes straight on and Taylor easily blocks it out.
The flatter one outside off, the batsman goes back and keeps it out.
Tossed up again on middle stump, Moor plays it towards mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery again on middle stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Moor defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Taylor flicks it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on off stump, Moor drives it towards mid off. The batsmen take a single.
Turns away from the batsman, Moor is completely beaten on this one.
Gives it air and bowls it around off, the batsman is solid in defense.
On the stumps, it is kept out.
A quick run! This is clipped towards mid-wicket for a run.
Fired on the leg pole. It turns back in slightly. Hits his thigh pad and then lobs towards his glove but unlike Chari's wicket this dies down onto the ground.
Flatter and on off, Moor uses his long reach and keeps it out.
Works it around the corner with the turn and takes a run. He moves on to 65.
Tossed up on off stump, Peter drives it towards mid off.
Flighted delivery again on middle stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Gives this a bit of air, Moor defends off the front foot.
Loopy delivery on off stump, the batsman blocks it out.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Moor keeps it out.
Tossed up on off stump, Moor drives it towards covers.
This is on the off pole, Taylor this time gets behind the line and blocks it out. A testing over from Mehidy.

BEAUTY! This is the advantage of bowling from around the wicket. The straighter ones are a threat to the outside edge and the ones that turn in can present an LBW opportunity. Mehidy this time angles it away from the off pole. Taylor plays inside the line as he felt it would turn back in. The ball goes straight on and beats the outside edge of the bat.
The batsman has played it to the point region.
Slower through the air on middle, Taylor with the turn works it to mid-wicket.
Flighted ball on off, this one goes on with the angle. Moor guides it through point, a run taken.
Slower through the air on middle, Moor lunges and defends it out.
Flatter and it is angled into the batsman, it is worked through mid-wicket for another run.
Gives it a little more air on off, Moor plants his front foot forward and strokes it down to long off for a single.
Another loopy ball on middle, Moor keeps it out off the front foot.
Tosses it up on middle, Moor lunges and defends it quite easily.
This is fired on middle and leg, sliding down, Moor tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads.
Flatter and a touch shorter on off, the batsman pushes it down to long off for a run.
Taijul Islam to bowl from the other end.
Gives it air on off, Moor keeps it out.
Very full on the pads, this is flicked through mid-wicket for a run. 200 up for Zimbabwe.
The arm ball is slanted away with the angle. Taylor tries to defend but the ball takes the outside edge and goes through short third man for a couple.
Floats it up on middle, Moor hits it down to long on for a run.
Once again it is in the leg stump line, Taylor goes back and works it behind square on the leg side. The batsmen go for a run. The fielder has a shy at the non-striker's end but misses.
Down the leg side, Taylor tries to flick but misses to get hit on the pads. It rolls towards short fine leg.

We are back, around 35 overs to go in the day, so we are in for a long session. Brendan Taylor and Peter Moor will resume their innings. Mehidy Hasan to bowl the first over after the break. Here we go...
... Day 3, Session 3 ...

A tremendous effort is what will be needed from the pair if Zimbabwe are to make a comeback in this game. Bangladesh, on the other hand, need their other bowlers to chip in with the wickets. It has been all Taijul for them till now and a little support won't harm. Another 128 runs needed to avoid the follow-on. Can Zimbabwe do so? Join us after the break to find out.

Another session which belongs to Bangladesh but Zimbabwe are fighting back, courtesy the pair of Taylor and Moor. They lost Williams and Raza quickly post-Lunch. Taijul Islam got the better of both. Taylor and Moor then formed an alliance and together they have really played well. The partnership currently is 64 runs and Taylor has brought up his half century as well. But the visitors are still not out of jail though.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Moor is on the back foot in defense. That will be Tea on Day 3!
FOUR! Flighted delivery on off stump, turning away, Moor drives it towards covers for a boundary. Nicely played with the spin, right through the gap, not much risk.
Tossed up on off stump, Moor defends off the front foot.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Moor defends off the front foot.
Tossed up outside off stump, Taylor drives it towards mid off. The batsmen take a single.
Length ball, but the batsman chooses to go onto his back foot and then punches the ball straight back to the bowler.
Similar delivery, Moor comes onto his front foot and defends it.
Fuller and slightly quicker ball outside off, Moor drives straight to the mid off fielder.
Flatter ball on the stumps, punched off the back foot by Moor. No run.
Quicker ball at a full length on off stump. Taylor drives it just to the left of short mid-wicket who dives and stops it but cannot prevent the single.
Flatter and quicker on off stump. Taylor defends it to short mid-wicket. No run.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Moor plays it off the front foot.
Quicker delivery on off stump, Moor defends off the back foot.
Tossed up again on middle stump, the batsman blocks it well.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Peter keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Taylor plays it towards mid on. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on middle stump, Moor plays it towards mid on. The batsmen take a single.
Fuller and flighted delivery. Taylor defends it watchfully.
That's a bouncer from a spinner! Moor stays up and on his back foot and plays the ramp shot over the slip. The batsmen pick  up three runs.

SIX! Huge one over deep square leg! Flighted delivery outside off, Moor goes down on one knee, picks the ball up and deposits over the square leg fence. Wonderful shot, that! It also brings up the 50-run stand between the two. Handy one but they need a lot more.
Flatter and outside off. Defended on the leg side. One run taken.
Flatter and quicker trajectory on off stump, defended by Taylor with a straight bat.
Flighted outside off stump, Moor gets to the pitch of the ball and drives it beautifully in the gap. A long chase for mid off who saves a run for his team.
Mahmudullah is into the attack.
Flighted delivery again on off stump, the batsman keeps it out.
Tossed up again on off stump, Taylor offers a forward defense on this one.
Loopy delivery on off stump, the batsman blocks it well.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Taylor defends off the back foot.
FOUR! Tossed up on middle stump, Taylor goes high and over mid on for a boundary.
Drifts away from the batsman, Taylor offers no shot.
Taijul Islam is back on.
Good length ball angling on to Taylor's pads, he flicks it away again in the air  and to deep backward square leg to pick up a single.
Short of a good length, Taylor goes onto his back foot and defends it.
Slightly fuller and outside off, driven to cover for a run.
Good length ball on off stump, Moor wants to defend but gets an inside edge onto his pads. No run.
FOUR! Short again outside off. Moor makes room and cuts it away beautifully in the gap, to the left of the point fielder, to pick up an easy boundary. Adjusted really nicely to play this shot.

Fifty for Taylor! Short and wide outside off, Taylor cuts it away towards point. The batsmen go for a tight run but the fielder makes it easier for them as he misses the ball and lets it through his feet. It could've been a tight call if he had picked it up cleanly. No harm done in the end and that single takes Taylor to his 9th fifty in this format. A well-compiled innings this and at a very important time for Zimbabwe. Lots of work to be done still though!
Flighted delivery on leg stump, the batsman plays it towards mid on. They take a single.
Loopy delivery again on middle stump, Taylor plays it towards mid on.
Tossed up again on middle stump, Brendan goes for a sweep but gets a top edge on this one. It goes towards fine leg. The batsmen pick up a couple.
Loopy delivery on leg stump, Taylor plays it towards mid-wicket.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Moor plays it towards mid on. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on middle stump, Taylor defends off the front foot and it goes past short leg. The batsmen take a single.
Short of a length, Moor takes his eyes of the ball while attempting to leave it. It hits him high on the arm and balloons up to forward short leg who appeals but the umpire isn't interested.
Full and outside off, Moor wants to drive it but can't connect as he'd desire. Just gets a bottom edge that goes straight back to the bowler.
Good ball to follow it up. On the stumps and it is defended with a straight bat back to the bowler.
Short and aimed at the body. It was an uncomfortable ball to play but Moor adjusts and defends it well in the end.
Length ball  on the stumps, Moor tries to defend but gets a thick inside edge that drops down on the leg side. No run.
Good length outside the off stump, safely played with soft hands by Taylor towards the point region. The batsmen run a single.
FOUR! Shot! This is tossed up outside off, it is a little too full. The spin is out of contention and Moor slaps it through covers for a boundary.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Moor defends off the back foot.
Tossed up on leg stump, Taylor sweeps it towards square leg. The batsmen take a single.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Brendan keeps it out.
Turns into the middle stump, Taylor defends off the back foot.

HUGE APPEAL FOR CAUGHT BEHIND! NOT OUT! Flighted delivery outside off stump, Taylor goes for the reverse sweep but gets beaten on this one. An appeal follows but the umpire shakes his head. Bangladesh then think about a review but opt against it and rightly so. Later on in the replays, there was a spike on Ultra Edge but it was mostly of the bat hitting the ground.
Mehidy Hasan is back into the attack.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off. Moor latches onto the opportunity, frees his arms and cuts it away hard, square on the off side for four runs.
Good length ball on the middle stump, Taylor plays it with a straight bat to long on for a single.
Length ball outside off stump, Taylor shoulders his arms to that one.
Good ball. Slightly fuller and angled in after pitching. Lucky for Taylor that it took the inside edge, else he would've been rapped in front of the wickets.
Length ball on the stumps, defended off the back foot.
Good length ball outside off stump. The batsman chooses to leave it alone.
Flighted delivery again on off stump, the batsman defends it watchfully to end the over.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Moor keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Peter blocks it well.
Tossed up on middle stump, Moor defends off the back foot.
FOUR! Consecutive boundaries for Peter Moor. Overpitched outside off stump, Moor drives it through covers for a boundary.
FOUR! Half tracker from Taijul, Moor pulls it over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Length ball on the pads this time. Moor misses the flick and it goes off the pads to fine leg for a leg bye.

Good length and angling into the pads this time, Taylor plays it in the air, dangerously close towards the backward short leg fielder. But unfortunately for Bangladesh, it is just a little too far away from him. It goes down to fine leg for a run.
Similar ball and similarly played as well.
Slightly short of a length, outside off. Jags back a bit after landing. Taylor adjusts and defends it watchfully.
Length ball on the stumps, defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Short of a length and going down the leg side. Taylor chooses to leave it alone. A good diving stop by Rahim.
Khaled Ahmed now has been given an opportunity to have a go.
Loopy delivery outside off stump, Moor offers no shot.
Tossed up again outside off stump, the batsman lets it go.
Flighted delivery again on off stump, Peter drives it towards point.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Moor defends off the front foot.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Taylor comes forward and plays it towards mid on. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on off stump, Taylor blocks it well.

Drinks! It has been all Bangladesh in the first hour of this session. Taijul Islam has spun a web around the Zimbabwe batsmen. He has four so far, of which, two have come in this session. Two big ones that is. The tourists are still a long way behind. The pair batting out there currently is probably their last hope. They will need a huge partnership from the two. Can they do so? Stay tuned to find out.
Coming around the wicket for the last ball before drinks in the post-Lunch session, Moor gets behind the line of the ball and plays it away safely.
Full delivery on the stumps, PJ Moor defends with a straight bat. No run.
Faster ball on the leg stump this time, Moor adjusts well to defend it.
Good length ball outside off. It was a cutter and Moor lets it go.
FOUR! Fuller this time and outside off, Moor drives and gets it in the gap between point and gully for a very welcome boundary.
BEATEN! Well bowled by Mustafizur. On a good length and in the corridor of uncertainty. Sticks in the wicket and moves very late to beat the outside edge of the batsman.

It appeared to be a bowling change as Khaled Ahmed is seen returning. A late call by Mahmudullah after that as he hands the ball once again to Mustafizur. Maybe because this will be the last over before the Drinks break.
Loopy delivery turning away from the batsman, Taylor manages to block it.
Tossed up on off stump, Moor drives it towards covers. The batsmen take a single.
Bangladesh on the attack here as they bring in another silly point fielder.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Peter keeps it out.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Moor gets a soft leading edge towards mid off.
Shorter on off stump, Moor cuts it towards point.
Not much turn on this one. Flighted delivery on middle stump, Moor blocks it well.
Solid defense on this occasion by Taylor. The ball was on middle stump, no problem for the batsman.
A cutter on a fuller length this time from the Fizz, goes past the outside edge of Taylor.
Good length ball on the off stump, Taylor wants to defend off the front foot but gets an inside edge onto the pads. It balloons up and then luckily for him it falls safely in the middle of the pitch.
Slightly short of a length on the off stump, Taylor defends on the back foot.
Good ball! Drags the length a little shorter than the previous ball but gets a better line. Taylor plays it with soft hands on the back foot.
Wayward ball on length outside off stump. Taylor leaves it alone.
Tossed up on off stump, Moor defends off the front foot. Maiden over from Taijul Islam.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Moor defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off stump, the batsman keeps it out.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Moor defends off the back foot.
Tossed up outside off stump, Moor drives it towards mid off.
Length ball on the stumps, Taylor defends like a rock off the front foot.
Back to over the wicket now. Good length ball outside off stump. Taylor lets it go through to Rahim and watches it all the way.
Just short of a good length on the off stump, slight away movement after pitching. Taylor adjusts pretty well and plays it all along the ground to gully.
Good length ball coming in with the angle, on the stumps. Taylor's defense is solid.
Fuller this time and a very slight hint of swing after landing. Taylor drives to mid off.
Full and wide outside off stump. Taylor drives straight to cover. No run.
On off, the batsman manages to block it out.
Peter Moor strides out to the middle.

OUT! Another one bites the dust! Taijul Islam is breathing fire here. This was a top, top delivery! Not a lot Raza could have done with that. Maybe, he could have been a little forward there. Now though it is too late. Islam pitches this around middle, Raza plays for the original trajectory but the ball straightens a touch, beats the outside edge and hits the stumps. Half the side is back in the hut for Zimbabwe as Raza walks back for a duck. They need another 192 to avoid the follow-on. Looks an uphill task from here. Talking about Taijul and his brilliance with this delivery. He got Sean with a straighter arm ball and this time since he bowled it from wide of the crease, Raza was outsmarted as he thought it will once again skid in with the angle. That wasn't the case and his footwork was also quite ordinary. What a series Taijul is having!
Floats it up on off, it is driven towards covers.
Loopy delivery on leg stump, Raza flicked it towards short leg.
Flighted delivery on off stump, the batsman defends off the front foot.
Tossed up outside off stump, Raza goes for the drive but keeps it out.

This is much better from the Fizz, good length outside off stump. He brings Taylor onto his front foot making him drive to cover. Could bring the edge into play with this angle if he gets some movement.
Around the wicket now, full length and on the stumps, Taylor plays it with a straight bat back to mid off. No run taken.
Overpitched and on the middle stump, Taylor flicks it away to mid-wicket for a couple of runs.
Slightly fuller outside off this time, Taylor plays a defensive shot off the front foot.
Similar to the previous delivery, watchfully defended again to short cover. No run.
Length ball just outside off, well defended by Taylor off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Tossed up again on off stump, Raza drives it towards covers.
Flighted delivery on off stump, the batsman drives it towards covers.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Raza wanted to defend but it turned away from him. He is completely beaten on this one.
Tossed up again on off stump, Sikandar cuts it towards point.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Raza defends off the front foot.
Tries the yorker length ball, Taylor is upto it and keeps it out with a solid defense.
Full length ball outside off stump, defended onto the ground by Taylor.
Slightly fuller on off stump, Taylor defends it straight off the front foot.

BEATEN! Good length ball just outside off stump, Taylor feeling for the ball misses it and survives. There was slight movement on that ball after landing. Might be a hint of reverse swing for the Fizz.
Full delivery outside off, driven by BT straight to short cover. No run.
Good length ball to start off with, at the stumps. Taylor defends but not very convincingly. Takes a slight inside edge and falls to the leg side.
Mustafizur Rahman is back on.
A loopy ball to end the over, it is kept out safely.
Sikandar Raza is the new man in.

OUT! BOWLED 'EM! Williams seems to have missed a straight ball there. He has misread the length completely. Islam tosses it up around off, it goes on with the arm. Williams pays the price for not picking the variation. Also, he should have been forward to this delivery but he tries playing it off the back foot. That brings his downfall. He misses and the ball shatters the off stump behind. An early wicket after the break for Bangladesh and it is a big one. Williams walks back without making an impact.
Floats it up on off, SW keeps it out.
Flatter on off, the batsman defends it off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Taylor drives it towards covers. The batsmen take a single.
FOUR! Beautiful shot. Tossed up on leg stump, Taylor lofts it over mid on for a boundary.
Good length delivery turning into the pads, Taylor plays it with the turn down to fine leg for an easy single.

The ball is suddenly bouncing off small cracks on the pitch. This one starts on a good length and jumps on Taylor but he plays it with soft hands and hence it drops safely out of reach of any close-in fielder.
Faster ball outside off stump, cut to deep point off the back foot by Williams. The batsmen run a quick single. Well-judged in the end.
Flatter and quicker at the stumps, defended off the back foot. No run.
Fuller length on off stump, played to long on with a straight bat for a run.
Around the wicket to the left-hander, flatter and angling into the pads, Williams flicks it onto the leg side and takes a single
Tossed up again on middle stump, Brendan blocks it well.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Taylor defends off the front foot.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Williams flicks it towards the leg side. The batsmen take a single.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Brendan drives it towards mid on. The batsmen take a single.
FOUR! Great shot. Flighted delivery on off stump, Taylor dances down the track and lofts it straight over the bowler for a boundary.
Tossed up on middle stump, Taylor blocks it well.

WOAH! What happened there? Must have hit a crack or something. This is bowled flatter and just outside off stump. It pitches and bounces out of nowhere, also turns to beat the outside edge of Williams. Lots of energy amongst the close-in fielders.
Flatter trajectory on this ball, Williams gets behind the ball and defends it safely.
Good length ball outside off, defended to mid on off the front foot.
Fuller and faster outside off stump this time, played watchfully onto the off side for a single.
Slightly tossed up outside off, Taylor immediately goes down and reverse sweeps it wide of the slip fielder to pick up a double.
Flatter and quicker ball outside off, played back down the ground off the back foot. No run.
Flighted delivery again on leg stump, Brendan flicks it towards the leg side. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up again on off stump, Taylor blocks it well.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, the batsman pushes it towards the leg side. The batsmen pick up a single.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Sean drives it towards long off.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Williams flicks it towards mid-wicket.
Tossed up on leg stump, Taylor plays it towards mid-wicket. The batsmen take a single.
FOUR! Short and wide outside off, Williams rocks back and cuts it away beautifully for a boundary.
Fuller delivery just outside off, the batsman pushes it to cover. No run.
Flatter and on the stumps. It bounces a little more. Williams defended off the back foot.
Flatter and on the pads, flicked away by BT behind square on the leg side for a run.
Flighted delivery on middle, driven to long on for a single.
Coming around the wicket to Sean Williams, flatter and outside off, Williams flicks to the leg side but hits short leg. No run.
Tossed up again on middle stump, Taylor defends off the back foot.
Mehidy Hasan to bowl from the other end.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Williams drives it towards covers. The batsmen take a single.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Williams defends off the back foot.
Tossed up on his pads, Brendan works it towards fine leg. The batsmen take a single.
Flighted delivery on leg stump, Taylor keeps it out.
Tossed up on middle stump, Taylor pushes it to short leg.

We're back for the afternoon session. The men concerned are back on the field as well. A very important next two hours for Zimbabwe. They need a big effort from two of their most experienced batsmen in the middle if they want to get anywhere near Bangladesh's first innings total. For Bangladesh, it's just about hitting the right areas and keep probing. They are beginning with the spin of Taijul Islam, as expected. Let's play...
... DAY 3, SECOND SESSION ...

The visitors still need another 223 to avoid the follow-on which will surely be their first aim. They have their two most reliable batsmen out there. The wicket is not doing much and a lot will be expected from them. Bangladesh, on the other hand, will want to get rid of these two as quickly as possible and then get into the lower order. What do we have in store for us in the second session? Join us in a while to find out.

Chari then continued to fight hard. He was hit on the head not once but twice but that did not deter his confidence. Those blows in a way woke him up and he excelled to score freely. He brought up his half ton and also stitched a 50-run stand with Taylor in which he scored majority of the runs. However, an excellent review from Bangladesh saw the end of him minutes before the break.

It is Bangladesh who head into the break as the happier side. Chari's wicket right at the stroke of Lunch has turned the tide in hosts' favor. The tourists started off really well with Chari and Tiripano grinding it out in the first hour. They almost managed to play out the first 60 minutes but Taijul Islam struck as he sent back the nightwatchman.
Another full one on middle and Williams pushes it to covers. No run taken. The umpire removes the bails and signals for Lunch on Day 3.
Full length again and angling into the pads, Williams takes his front leg out of the way and defends it watchfully.
Full and outside off, Williams drives to cover. No run.
Fullish length outside off, Taylor plays it to the vacant leg side region for a single. 100 up for Zimbabwe!
Slightly shorter length, Taylor goes on to his back foot and defends watchfully.
Good length and outside off stump, Taylor gets an inside edge on to his pads but it safely drops down on the pitch.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Taylor gets an inside edge onto his pads. It goes towards the leg side. The batsmen take a single.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Williams drives it towards mid on. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on off stump, Williams goes for the cut but misses as the ball stays low.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Williams plays it straight towards the bowler.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Brendan plays it towards mid off. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on off stump, Taylor defends off the front foot.
Tosses it up on off, Williams is solid in defense.
Flatter and on off, kept out.
Sean Williams is the new man in.

OUT! Yes, Ultra Edge shows some spike, which means it has just about flicked the glove. Chari has to walk back minutes before Lunch. He is not happy, not sure with the decision or with the mode of the dismissal. This is bowled down the leg side, Chari looks to pad it away but the ball hits him on the thigh pad and then lobs up and goes extremely close to his gloves. Mominul at short leg takes it and appeals. The umpire shakes his head. The fielder though feels there is something and he wants it to be reviewed. Mahmudullah does so. Time for the replays and it shows a spike as the ball passes the glove. Although, it's a bit uncertain that the spike is exactly after the ball is kissing the glove or it is due to his left leg scratching the surface. The third umpire feels it has brushed the gloves and the on-field call has been overturned. Excellent review by Bangladesh and they have got the well-set batsman out. Also, the partnership which was starting to look good has been cut short. Zimbabwe in a spot of bother. They need another 227 runs to avoid the follow-on.
Review time! A loud appeal for a catch at short leg has been turned down. Mahmudullah has signaled the 'T'. Has it taken the glove?

Good ball, slightly shorter than the previous two balls, Chari is in two minds whether to come ahead or not and decides to play it off the back foot. It takes his thigh pad on the way and travels to leg slip. Excitement for the bowler and close-in fielders but there seemed to be nothing on it. The fielder at leg slip doesn't take it so the excitement eventually dies out.
Similar ball and similarly defended again.
Good length ball on middle. Chari comes ahead and defends.
Tossed up on off stump, Brian drives it towards mid off. The batsmen take a single.
Loopy delivery again on middle stump, Chari again keeps it out.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, the batsman keeps it out.
Loopy delivery on off stump, Chari defends off the front foot.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Brian plays it towards covers.
Tossed up on middle stump, Chari blocks it well.

FOUR! That's another brilliant sweep shot from Taylor! Sean Williams (earlier in the day in an interview) had suggested that it would be a shot that they would go to today and his teammate is proving him right! Full and wide outside off but Taylor goes down and takes it from there and finds the square leg boundary.
Full and outside off, defends it well this time.

LOUD APPEAL! Full ball outside off, Taylor attempts the reverse sweep again but misses it. It seems to have struck him outside the line. After a long consultation with Rahim, Mahmudullah decides not to go upstairs.
Shorter ball at the stumps, Brendan defends it off the back foot to short leg.
Full and outside off but Taylor sweeps it in the gap between deep square leg and deep mid wicket. The batsmen pick up two. It also brings up the 50-run partnership between the pair.
Good length ball outside off, Taylor comes forward and defends it well.
Well fielded! This is driven nicely towards covers. The fielder there dives to his right and makes a very good stop.
Another flighted ball on off, Chari lunges and defends it onto the ground.
On the shorter side and there is width on offer, Chari guides it to point.
Quicker and flatter again on off, Chari is quickly onto his back foot and keeps it out.
Flatter and slightly shorter in length, Chari goes back and defends it onto the ground.
Floats it up on off, the batsman lunges and defends it.
Similar length but outside off this time, Taylor defends it but gets a thick edge that drops on to the off side. No run.
Shorter in length this time, Taylor goes onto his back foot and defends to short mid-wicket.
Full outside off, the batsman gets behind the line of the ball and defends it well.
FOUR! Full ball outside off, Taylor goes down on one knee and reverse sweeps it for four runs through backward point. The runs seem to be flowing now!
Slightly shorter this time, BT goes onto his back foot and defends with a straight bat.
Good ball to start, outside off and drawing the batsman on to the front foot. But Taylor defends it well. No turn on that one.
Bowling change. Mehidy Hasan has the ball in his hand.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Brian defends off the back foot.

FOUR! Fifty for Brian Chari. His second in this format. He did cop a few blows but has really battled hard out there. However, his job is still not done and he would surely know that. Chari would love to score a big one here. Good shot from him to get to the landmark. It is a flighted delivery on middle stump, Chari lofts it straight over the bowler for a boundary.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Brian keeps it out.

FOUR! Beautiful shot. Consecutive boundaries for Brian Chari. Tossed up on off stump, Chari lofts this over covers. The umpire checks whether it went all the way but after getting the confirmation, he signals for a boundary.
FOUR! Great Shot. Flighted delivery on middle stump, Brian lofts it straight down the ground for a boundary.
Tossed up on leg stump, Chari keeps it out.

Oooh and Aahs from behind the stumps as this one keeps low. It was a length ball outside off but it keeps low as Taylor tries to punch it off the back foot. It gets the under edge and just drops down on the pitch.
Length ball outside off, defended watchfully by Taylor.
Good length ball on off stump, played with a straight bat from within the crease by Taylor. No run.

LOUD APPEAL! The umpire says not out, presumably because of the height of the ball. The replays suggest it would've gone over the stumps. Good decision by Bangladesh to not review that one. This one starts just outside off stump, comes in after landing on a good length area and hits him in line of the stumps but the height was a little too much for the hosts liking.
Just short of a good length, at the hips. Taylor tucks it off his hips and luckily for him, it lands just short of a backward short leg fielder who's been placed there exactly for that.
Short ball first up, outside off. BT just ducks and lets it go through.
FOUR! Good shot. Tossed up again on leg stump, Chari sweeps it through square leg for a boundary.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Brian defends off the back foot.
HUGE APPEAL FOR LBW! NOT OUT! Tossed up delivery, Chari goes for the sweep but misses it and gets rapped on the pads. The umpire shakes his head. Pitched outside leg.
Loopy delivery around off stump, Chari defends on the front foot.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Brendan hits it straight past the bowler towards long off. The batsmen take a single.
Tossed up on middle stump, Taylor blocks it well.
Good response from the debutant after being hit for a six on the previous ball. Gets in a really good yorker on middle but equally well played and kept out by Chari.
SIX! These blows seem to have woken up Chari! He is seeing the ball really well now and deposits this short one from Khaled for a maximum over deep square leg. Brilliant execution of the shot!
Taylor looks a bit uncomfortable here as this one jags in sharply after landing on the pitch, takes the inside edge and runs behind square on the leg side for a single.
Length ball on the off stump. Defended watchfully by Taylor.

Good movement after pitching! The ball starts outside off stump but moves inward by a long way after passing the stumps. Although it's left alone safely, the batsman would be keeping a close eye from now onward.
Good length ball but at the pads, Taylor plays it with soft hands to short mid-wicket. No run.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, the batsman defends off the back foot.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Brian plays it towards point.
Tossed up again on off stump, Chari defends off the front foot.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Brendan pushes it towards the leg side. The batsmen take a single.
Flighted delivery on off stump, Taylor defends on the front foot towards covers.
Tossed up outside off stump, Taylor lets it go.
A huge appeal but not given! Height was an issue there. This is bowled on a length on middle, it jags back in. Chari tries to flick but misses to get hit high on the pads.

FOUR BYES! Loses his radar completely there. Bangs it short but it is way down the leg side. Maybe he tried a little too hard there. Rahim had no chance to stop that and the ball races to the fine leg fence.
FOUR! So Chari has now scored 10 from the last two balls he has faced. This was pure timing. A little too full on off, Chari pushes it through mid off and the ball races away.
A little too straight this time and it is worked towards fine leg for a run.
Closer to the off pole this time and it is slightly fuller on off, the batsman blocks it out.
Off the mark is Taylor with this punch shot. It goes through covers and the batsmen take two.
SIX! Great Shot. Tossed up on off stump, Chari lofts it over mid off and it goes over the boundary for a six.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Brian keeps it out.
Loopy delivery on middle stump, Chari blocks it well.
Tossed up again on off stump, Chari offers a forward defense on this one.
Flighted delivery on middle stump, Brian blocks it well.
Tossed up on middle stump, Chari defends off the front foot.

DROPPED! Chari seems to have lost concentration after the blow and slashes wildly at a wide one outside off. It's in the air and goes towards Taijul Islam at backward point who dives to catch it but can't hold on. Wasn't that tough and should hold onto these ones at this level. The batsmen run through for a single.
The physio is out once again and is examining Chari. The opener seems fine. He's getting habituated in copping such blows. Drinks on the field.

OUCH! Second time in this innings, Chari looks to duck but takes his eyes off the ball and gets hit on the helmet. He will surely have to change his helmet this time! Short ball on middle, doesn't bounce as much as the batsman expects it to and hits the helmet again.
Good pace from the youngster, short of a good length and angling into the hips, nicely negotiated by Chari and tucked away behind square leg for a couple of runs.

Short of a good length, angling down the leg side, Chari raises his arms to let the ball go but the ball hits his hips and rolls away to the fine leg boundary. But the umpire signals dead ball as there was no shot attempted.

Just as I say that there was good carry on the previous ball, the next one keeps pretty low. On off stump and a good length and the batsman does well to block it out even though he is on his back foot.
Good length outside off stump, Chari leaves it alone. Good carry on that occasion.
Khaled Ahmed is back on. Change of ends for him.

We are all set for the action to begin. Out come Brian Chari and Donald Tiripano who will resume their innings. The former will be on strike and he will face Khaled Ahmed who will start the proceedings for Bangladesh. Here we go...

Mushfiqur Rahim's turn now to give a little interview. He starts by crediting Mominul for the way he batted. Wants to start well today and hopes his bowlers put up a good show. Reckons it is very important to show character and patience, especially when the team needs it. Ends by saying that winning this Test match is the main focus.

Sean Williams, who is giving an interview, says he feels pretty good this morning but a few players will be tired as they bowled 160 overs. Reckons patience is the key. Credits the way Rahim batted. Further adds he used the depth of his crease well and played nicely. Mentions the sweep shot will be used a lot by them. States runs are not going to be easy to come and they will have to work hard for it. Ends by saying it will be amazing to bat around the same overs as Bangladesh did and hopefully a batsman or two can cross the three-digit mark.

Pitch report - Tino Mawoyo reminds that there was a little bit of variable bounce yesterday afternoon, however, it is not too much of a concern as it is outside the off stump. Reckons it is sticking in the surface a little and the Zimbabwe batters need to play a touch late.

The tourists, on the other hand, need their experienced players to step up here. They have a daunting task ahead of them and their batters need to bat out of their skin if they are to wipe off the deficit or even come close. There was not a lot of turn yesterday but one would expect the ball to do a lot more today. Will we see Zimbabwe fight back or will Bangladesh continue their dominance?

Hello and welcome to Day 3 which is often termed as the moving day of a Test match. The hosts are in a strong position and they would look to drive home the advantage. They would try and bundle the tourists' batsmen out cheaply and then hope to enforce the follow-on.
... Day 3, Session 1 ...

Okay then! Trail by 497 runs. 9 wickets in the bank. Will Zimbabwe manage to get past the follow-on mark? They need another 298 runs. Batting the whole of Day 3 might help them achieve that. On the other hand, with the pitch expected to turn even more on Tuesday, the Bangladesh spinners will be licking their lips. Join us at 9.30 am local (0330 GMT) for all the action from Day 3. ADIOS! TAKE CARE!

With 18 overs left in the day, Zimbabwe had a difficult task in hand against the fading light. But the openers showed a lot of patience before Hamilton Masakadza edged one, which was not taken. However, just when it seemed like no wicket will fall in the final session, the tourists lost their skipper, Hamilton Masakadza, which was a big blow.

But the man of the moment was Mushfiqur Rahim. His unbeaten 219 made him the first player to score a double ton this year and also the first wicket-keeper to score twin double tons in Test cricket. His score was also the best by a Bangladesh batsman, going past his teammate Shakib Al Hasan. It was a perfect scenario for Bangladesh - Bat first, bat once, bat big. Which they did.

Building on the overnight score of 303/5, Rahim and captain Mahmdullah took charge and played patiently as the new ball was swinging a bit. Zimbabwe bowled well during that time but were unlucky not to get any wickets. Jarvis was again brilliant, taking five wickets.
End of a dull day of cricket. A dominating display from Bangladesh. They will be happy going into the dressing room with a wicket at the fag end of the day.
